optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Backend API Engineer, Equipment Maintenance Services

professionalSummary.text: Developed and maintained the work-order API (Go) and parts-availability service for the technician app, implementing idempotency keys to prevent duplicate work orders from sync retries.
professionalSummary.witness: Developed and maintained the work-order API (Go) and the parts-availability service that queries depot stock for the technician app, including the idempotency keys added so that retried syncs did not create duplicate work orders.

professionalSummary.text: Owned and maintained integration test suites for both services, adding replay tests from anonymized sync logs to keep tests green in CI.
professionalSummary.witness: Owned the integration test suite for both services, adding replay tests built from anonymised sync logs and keeping the suite passing in the CI pipeline.

professionalSummary.text: Maintained API change logs and on-call hand-over checklists for every release, noting depot stock refresh intervals.
professionalSummary.witness: Kept the API change log current, noting for each release that depot stock was refreshed only hourly, and maintained the on-call hand-over checklist.

professionalSummary.text: Coordinated releases with app and platform teams through release reviews, though deployments were executed by the platform team's release engineer.
professionalSummary.witness: Lined up each release with the app team and the platform team in the release review; deployments to production were run by the platform team's release engineer, not by me.

experienceHighlights.text: Two and a half years on the service-platform team managing work-order and parts services, integration tests, release coordination, and API documentation.
experienceHighlights.witness: Two and a half years on the service-platform team: work-order and parts services, integration tests, release line-up and the change log.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Replay tests for work-order API and API change log entry for one release, with CI run numbers for traceability.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the replay tests for the work-order API and one release's entry in the API change log; CI run numbers are included so they can be traced.

skills.text: Go programming, API design, integration testing, release coordination, documentation maintenance.
skills.witness: Developed and maintained the work-order API (Go) and the parts-availability service... Owned the integration test suite... Lined up each release... Kept the API change log current...

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The materials establish the candidate's direct involvement in developing and maintaining the work-order API and parts-availability service, owning integration tests, coordinating releases, and maintaining documentation. However, the materials do not establish a measurable reduction in work-order sync failures as required by req_a43cb3667b39, relying instead on a reference call that cites support-ticket volume rather than the platform's documented metric.

decisionBoundary.statement: Human review required due to insufficient evidence for req_a43cb3667b39 (measurable reduction in sync failures) and a reference call that does not align with the platform's documented metric.

evidence.text: Developed and maintained the work-order API (Go) and the parts-availability service that queries depot stock for the technician app, including the idempotency keys added so that retried syncs did not create duplicate work orders.
Owned the integration test suite for both services, adding replay tests built from anonymised sync logs and keeping the suite passing in the CI pipeline.

Reference call with former engineering manager: said the idempotency change 'basically made the duplicate problem go away' and guessed sync failures dropped 'from a few hundred a week to a handful'; he said he was going by support-ticket volume rather than the platform's sync-failure metric.
evidence.notes: Reference call cites support-ticket volume, not platform metric.
